correctness.rationale: The horizontal and vertical coordinate steps give precisely twelve distinct transpositions. The connected site graph generates all permutations; parity changes with each move, and token relabeling gives transitivity. An independent exact layer traversal packs each placement into nine four-bit fields, swaps fields by XOR, and constructs each next set as all legal neighbors not yet seen. Induction makes each layer the set at its stated minimum distance. Enumeration reaches all 9! placements, reproduces every claimed layer, and terminates with only 876543210 at depth 16. Relabeling the identity by p transports that last state to p composed on the right with the positional half-turn. This involution has no fixed configuration and pairs the states, giving 181440 unordered diametral pairs; transitivity gives radius 16. Each swap moves two tokens one edge and hence can reduce the total Manhattan distance by at most two. Computing the bound on every reached state reproduces the full six-bin excess distribution, with twenty maximizing states at excess five.
residual_risks: This is an exhaustive finite certificate for the specified graph, not an extrapolation or an analysis of larger, blank-tile, or parallel models.

value.rationale: The established Swap Game is a natural fixed routing benchmark rather than an arbitrary subset of states. The all-state diameter gives its exact worst routing budget, while the unique half-turn identifies the configuration needed to test the extremal case. The second census independently measures sharp error of a standard lower bound (including the number of maximizers), giving exact benchmarks for pruning and lower-bound improvements beyond rerunning one known puzzle input. Value belongs to these precise invariants, not to the textbook use of BFS.
residual_risks: The method is standard exhaustive search, and the results give neither a new routing algorithm nor larger-grid asymptotics.
